meta.description: From identity verification to spending: the five steps to obtain and use crypto-collateralized credit on Hentsch Credit.

HowItWorks.title: How it works
HowItWorks.description: From identity verification to spending, in five steps.

kyc.title: 1. Identity verification (KYC)
kyc.description: By invitation only: your identity is verified before any access to deposits or credit, with no exceptions.

deposit.title: 2. Deposit your collateral
deposit.description: Stablecoins, tokenized precious or industrial metals, or ETH, on the Ethereum network.

credit.title: 3. Credit granted automatically
credit.description: 350% of the amount deposited, unlocked as soon as your request is validated (minus a 2% origination fee, charged once).

spend.title: 4. Spend with your card
spend.description: Use your credit line internally or directly with your bank card.

repay.title: 5. Repay to release the collateral
repay.description: Up to 60% repaid automatically by the collateral's yield; the rest by personal contribution. Conversely, a sharp drop in the collateral's value can lead to its liquidation.

HowItWorks.feesNote: The detail of the real rates and fees lives on the <pricing>Pricing</pricing> page, and the detail of automatic repayment, including the liquidation risk in the event of a sharp drop in the collateral's value, on the <yield>Yield</yield> page.

kyc.title: 1. Identity verification
kyc.body: Access is by invitation only. Once your account request is accepted, an account and a temporary password are communicated to you offline, then your identity is verified before any other operation. As long as this status is not confirmed, generating a deposit address and any credit request are technically blocked, not just discouraged.

deposit.title: 2. Depositing the collateral
deposit.body: Depending on the asset chosen, the deposit address provided is either individual (credited automatically as soon as it's confirmed on-chain) or pooled between clients (you declare your deposit, an advisor validates it manually once the funds are actually received). The corresponding credit is issued automatically as soon as the available balance reaches the amount requested, with no additional manual intervention on our part.

credit.title: 3. Credit issuance
credit.body: 350% of the amount deposited, at the rate in effect at the time of lock-in: a position already locked in always keeps this rate, even if the ratio later changes for new clients. The origination fee (2%) is charged only once, on the credit issued, not on your collateral.

usage.title: 4. Using the credit
usage.body: The credit granted is only a ceiling: no interest or repayment is due as long as you don't actually use it (card payment, internal use). It's a revolving credit line, not a loan paid out all at once into your available balance.

repayment.title: 5. Repayment
repayment.body: Two channels, daily and automatic for the first: the real appreciation of your collateral (up to 60% of the credit issued), and your personal contribution for the rest. Full repayment releases your collateral, which becomes withdrawable again. Conversely, a severe depreciation of the collateral (50% since it was deposited) leads to its liquidation, without erasing the credit already used.

kycRejected.question: What happens if my KYC is rejected?
kycRejected.answer: No financial operation is possible as long as the status is not verified. In the event of rejection, the company may refuse, suspend or close the account concerned, particularly in case of doubt about the declared identity.

approvalDelay.question: How long does approval of a credit request take?
approvalDelay.answer: It varies depending on back-office workload: a request goes through a manual validation queue before it can receive a deposit. The credit itself is issued automatically as soon as the funds are received, with no additional delay once the request is approved.

earlyWithdrawal.question: Can I withdraw my collateral before repaying everything?
earlyWithdrawal.answer: No. Locked collateral remains blocked as long as the corresponding used credit has not been fully repaid. Only the available balance, excluding locked collateral, can be freely withdrawn at any time.

s1.body: The site has not yet undergone a formal accessibility audit (of the RGAA or WCAG type). It therefore cannot be declared compliant with a specific level. Efforts are nonetheless already applied in the design: semantic page structure, heading hierarchy, colour contrasts designed for readability, and keyboard navigation possible on the main journeys (login, account request, viewing the account).

s2.item2: No independent audit has been carried out by a third-party body specialised in digital accessibility;
s2.item3: Certain third-party content (for example webhooks and external provider interfaces integrated into the platform) is not under the direct control of {legalName}.

Archives.title: Archives
Archives.description: The evolution of the platform's main rules since its launch, in chronological order.

nonRetroactivity.title: Non-retroactivity of changes in terms
nonRetroactivity.detail: A change to the credit ratio, rate or threshold never applies to a position already locked in: it keeps the terms granted to it at creation, until it's repaid or matures. This principle has never changed since the platform launched.

step2.title: First ratio increase
step2.detail: 75% → 150% of the amount pledged, for new lock-ins.

step3.title: Second ratio increase
step3.detail: 150% → 200% of the amount pledged, for new lock-ins.

step4.title: Credit ratio in effect
step4.detail: 200% → 350% of the amount pledged, for new lock-ins.

step5.title: Extension of accepted collateral assets
step5.detail: Addition of ETH and SHIB, then tokenized silver (KAG), alongside stablecoins.

step6.title: Extension to industrial metals and commodities
step6.detail: Addition of platinum (XPT), palladium (XPD), copper (XCU) and synthetic oil (WTI), as part of the RWA strategy.

step7.title: Automatic repayment via collateral yield
step7.detail: Introduction of automatic repayment through the real appreciation of the collateral, capped at 60% of the credit issued; the rest remains the client's responsibility.

step8.title: Indicative yield target on industrial RWA assets
step8.detail: Addition of an indicative target of 8 to 14% annualised on platinum, palladium, copper and synthetic oil only. This target remains indicative: it is neither guaranteed nor used in the calculation of the credit granted.

step9.title: Introduction of the liquidation mechanism
step9.detail: Introduction of an alert threshold (30% depreciation of the collateral since it was deposited) and a liquidation threshold (50%). Details are on the Yield page and in the terms and conditions, section 7.

step10.title: Move to an automatically calculated estimated yield
step10.detail: The client credit simulators now calculate the estimated yield, the monthly payment and the first repayment date from real performance over the past 12 months, rather than asking the client to enter an estimate.

Archives.note: The currently applicable values (ratio, rates, fees, yield cap, liquidation thresholds) are detailed with their exact figures on the <link>Pricing</link> page. This archives page only traces the history of changes, not the terms applicable to your current position.

Cookies.title: Cookie policy
Cookies.intro: This page describes the cookies actually set by the Hentsch Credit platform and why no preference centre is offered.

s1.title: 1. What the platform sets
s1.body: Only one cookie is used, a session cookie, strictly necessary for the service to function: it keeps you authenticated while you browse the client area. It is deleted when you close your session or your browser.

s2.title: 2. What the platform does not set

s3.title: 3. Why there is no "manage my cookies"
s3.body: A preference centre makes sense when a site sets non-essential cookies (advertising, audience measurement) that require your prior consent and a way to withdraw it. The platform sets none: there is therefore no preference to turn on or off beyond your own browser's settings. If this ever changes, this page will be updated and a genuine preference centre will be offered, rather than a button with no real effect.

s4.title: 4. Control from your browser
s4.body: You can block or delete the session cookie at any time from your browser's settings. Blocking this particular cookie will log you out of the client area: it's a functional cookie, not a tracker, and it has no other role.

s5.title: 5. Contact
s5.body: For any question about this policy, contact the Data Protection Officer at {dpo}. The processing of other personal data is described in the <link>privacy policy</link>.

meta.title: Terms and conditions · Hentsch Credit
meta.description: The terms and conditions of use of the Hentsch Credit platform: credit, collateral, repayment, liquidation and fees.

Terms.title: Terms and conditions
Terms.intro: These terms and conditions govern access to and use of the Hentsch Credit platform, a credit service secured by digital assets, offered to a limited number of the company's clients by invitation. By opening an account, the client declares that they have read and accepted them.

s1.title: 1. Purpose
s1.body: {tradingName} allows a verified and previously invited client to deposit stablecoins or tokenized gold as collateral ("pledge"), and to obtain in return a credit line, usable internally and with an associated bank card. The service is provided by {legalName}, an independent asset manager (IAM) within the meaning of FinIA, in collaboration with licensed third-party depositary and custody institutions (see section 5).

s2.title: 2. Restricted access and eligibility
s2.body: The platform is not open to the public. Access is reserved for a list of clients determined by {legalName}, by invitation, as part of an existing wealth management relationship. Opening an account, generating a deposit address, any deposit of collateral and any granting of credit are further subject to prior verification of the client's identity ("KYC"). As long as the client's verification status is not confirmed, these operations are refused. The company reserves the right to refuse, suspend or close an account in the event of failure or doubt regarding this verification, or suspicion of fraud, money laundering or terrorist financing.

s3.title: 3. Assets accepted as collateral
s3.body: The following stablecoins are accepted as collateral, valued at par (1:1 USD): DAI, USDT, USDC; the following euro-pegged stablecoin, valued at the live spot price: dEURO; the following tokenized precious metals, also valued at the live spot price: XAUT (gold), KAG (silver); the following tokenized industrial metals and commodities, valued at the live spot price: XPT (platinum), XPD (palladium), XCU (copper), WTI (synthetic oil); as well as the following native cryptocurrencies, valued at the live spot price and subject to their own volatility: ETH, SHIB. These assets are accepted exclusively on the Ethereum network. For some assets, the deposit address provided is individual to each client; for others, it is pooled between clients and the declared deposit is subject to manual validation before being credited. The list of accepted assets, supported networks or the address mechanism applicable to each asset may be changed at any time, with no retroactive effect on positions already established.

s4.title: 4. Credit mechanism and collateral rate
s4.body1: When collateral is locked in, credit is granted equal to 350% of the amount pledged, at the rate in effect at the time of lock-in. The account's total purchasing power is calculated as follows:
s4.formula: Total purchasing power = Available balance + Locked collateral + Granted credit − Used credit
s4.body2: The applicable collateral rate is the one in effect at the time of each new lock-in. Any subsequent change to this rate does not retroactively affect credit already granted for collateral locked in previously: that credit remains subject to the terms of the time.
s4.body3: Credit issued on eligible collateral (tokenized precious metals, tokenized industrial metals and commodities, ETH) may be repaid up to a maximum of 60% through the real appreciation observed on that collateral, applied automatically to the credit used. The remaining 40% must be repaid through the client's personal contribution (deposit or explicit transfer). This cap applies to the amount of credit issued when the position was opened and is not recalculated if the credit ratio is later changed.
s4.body4: An indicative yield target (currently 8 to 14% per year) is communicated for information purposes on tokenized industrial metals and commodities (platinum, palladium, copper, synthetic oil): it reflects the target of the company's own treasury strategy on these assets (arbitrage, collateralized lending, liquidity provision), and not a guaranteed or contractual rate. This target has no effect on the calculation of the client's credit, which remains governed exclusively by the mechanism described in the previous paragraph.

s6.title: 6. Blocking of collateral and withdrawal
s6.body: The amount pledged and locked in cannot be withdrawn as long as the corresponding used credit has not been fully repaid. Only the available balance, excluding blocked collateral, can be freely withdrawn at any time, subject to applicable compliance controls.

s7.title: 7. Liquidation of collateral
s7.intro: Collateral whose value moves with the market (tokenized precious metals, tokenized industrial metals and commodities, ETH) is subject to daily monitoring of its value, compared with its value at the time of lock-in:
s7.item1: in the event of a depreciation of at least 30% from this entry value, an alert is recorded on the account, with no other effect;
s7.item2: in the event of a depreciation of at least 50%, the collateral is automatically removed from the account (liquidated) at its entry value.
s7.body: Liquidation of collateral does not extinguish the credit already used against that collateral: that credit remains fully due by the client, no longer covered by the collateral originally pledged. Liquidated collateral can no longer be returned, even if the price of the asset concerned subsequently recovers. The thresholds mentioned above may be changed at any time, with no retroactive effect on the assessment of a depreciation already observed.

s8.title: 8. Bank card and use of credit
s8.body: A bank card, issued by a licensed third-party partner, may be linked to the account to use the credit line granted, within the limit of the available credit (credit granted minus credit already used). Any transaction exceeding this limit is refused. The specific terms for issuing, using and blocking the card are set out in the specific conditions associated with it.

s9.title: 9. Repayment
s9.body: The client may repay all or part of the used credit at any time. Full repayment of the used credit against a given collateral releases that collateral, which becomes withdrawable again. The repayment simulators made available on the platform (flexible projection, fixed instalments) are provided for indicative purposes only: they are based on a yield estimated from past performance, which is no guide to future performance, and constitute neither a contractual commitment nor an enforceable payment schedule.

s10.title: 10. Fees
s10.body: The fees and rates currently applied are: an origination fee of 2.0%, charged once on the credit issued at the time the collateral is locked in; a collateral custody fee of 0.5% per year, on the amount of locked collateral; and interest on the credit used of 13.5% per year in USD (12.0% per year in EUR), made up of a monetary reference rate (SOFR for USD, EURIBOR for EUR) and an 8.5-point risk premium, justified by the platform's high credit ratio (350%). The up-to-date detail of this pricing is on the platform's Pricing page. These rates may be updated at any time, with no retroactive effect on positions already established: the rate structure fixed at the time a position is locked in remains in effect until it's repaid or matures.

s11.title: 11. Risks
s11.intro: The client acknowledges and accepts the risks inherent to digital assets, in particular:
s11.item1: the volatility of the price of assets valued at spot price (tokenized gold), which may affect the value of the collateral and the account's total purchasing power;
s11.item2: the risk of collateral liquidation in the event of severe depreciation (see section 7), which does not extinguish credit already used;
s11.item3: counterparty risk and operational risk linked to the depositary institutions and third-party custody providers mentioned in section 5;
s11.item4: regulatory risk linked to changes in the legal framework applicable to digital assets and stablecoins.
s11.body: These terms constitute neither investment advice nor a recommendation to buy, sell or hold any digital asset.

s16.title: 16. Direct investment
s16.intro: Distinct from collateralized credit (section 4) and direct credit, direct investment is a placement: the client locks up funds from their available balance in exchange for a return, with no credit issued and no collateral required.
s16.body1: The capital placed is neither guaranteed nor insured. The daily return applied reflects real market data and can be negative, which may reduce the position's value below the capital originally placed. The indicative return targets communicated to the client are never a performance commitment.
s16.body2: The return on the “RWA strategy” basket reflects the operator's real treasury-strategy performance on tokenized industrial metals and commodities; the return on the “Stocks” basket reflects the real movement of a basket of listed stocks, measured via a third-party market data provider.
s16.body3: The client may request the full withdrawal of their position at any time, with no notice or penalty; no partial withdrawal is offered at this stage.

s12.title: 12. Termination
s12.body: The client may close their account at any time, subject to full repayment of any credit used. The company may suspend or terminate access to the service in the event of a breach of these terms, suspicion of fraud or money laundering, or for any legal or regulatory reason.

s13.title: 13. Liability
s13.body: The company implements reasonable means to ensure the availability and security of the platform, with no guarantee of a total absence of interruption. Its liability cannot be engaged in the event of force majeure, malfunction of a blockchain network or of a third-party provider beyond its control, within the limits permitted by applicable Swiss law.

s14.title: 14. Amendment of the terms and conditions
s14.body: The company may amend these terms and conditions at any time, subject to prior notice to the client through the usual means of communication. Amendments have no retroactive effect on credit positions already established, unless otherwise required by law.

s15.title: 15. Applicable law and jurisdiction
s15.body: These terms and conditions are governed by Swiss law. Any dispute relating to their validity, interpretation or performance falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of {jurisdiction}, subject to applicable mandatory legal provisions.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.intro: This policy describes how H. Hentsch Asset Management SA collects, uses and protects the personal data of Hentsch Credit clients, a platform reserved for a limited clientele, in accordance with Swiss federal data protection law (nFADP) and, where applicable, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

s1.title: 1. Data controller
s1.compliance: Compliant with Swiss FADP and GDPR.

s2.title: 2. Data collected
s2.item1: Identification and contact data (name, email, contact details);
s2.item2: Identity verification documents and data (KYC) submitted when opening an account;
s2.item3: Data relating to deposit addresses, on-chain transactions and operations carried out on the platform (deposits, collateral lock-ins, credit grants, repayments, card payments);
s2.item4: Technical connection data to the platform (logs, session identifiers).

s3.title: 3. Purposes and legal basis
s3.item1: Performance of the contractual relationship: opening and managing the account, granting and monitoring credit, issuing and managing the associated bank card;
s3.item2: Compliance with legal and regulatory obligations: identity verification (KYC), combating money laundering and terrorist financing (AMLA), retention of accounting records;
s3.item4: Communication with the client relating to their account and their operations.

s4.title: 4. Partners and subcontractors
s4.intro: To perform the service, {legalName} uses specialised providers, who process certain data on its behalf and under its instructions, or who act as separate controllers for asset custody:
s4.item1Body: custody of clients' cash and securities (see legal notice, section 3);
s4.item2Body: secure custody of the stablecoins and tokenized gold deposited as collateral;
s4.item4Body: verification of the client's identity and compliance status;
s4.item5Body: detection of on-chain deposits and real-time asset prices.
s4.outro: The name, exact role and country of establishment of each provider used in production are communicated to the client on request from the department indicated in section 1.

s5.title: 5. Retention period
s5.body: Data relating to clients and their operations is retained for the duration of the management relationship, then for the duration required by applicable legal retention obligations (in particular accounting documents and transaction supporting evidence).

s6.title: 6. International transfers
s6.body: Some providers mentioned in section 4 may process data outside Switzerland. In that case, {legalName} puts in place the appropriate safeguards required by Swiss data protection legislation (contractual clauses, adequacy decision or equivalent mechanism).

s7.title: 7. Your rights
s7.body: Subject to the restrictions provided for by law (in particular applicable legal retention obligations), the client has a right of access, rectification, erasure and objection regarding their personal data. These rights may be exercised by writing to the address indicated in section 1.

s8.title: 8. Cookies and trackers
s8.body: The platform only uses cookies that are strictly necessary for it to function (session authentication, display preferences). No advertising or third-party audience-measurement cookie is set without the client's prior consent. Details are in the <link>cookie policy</link>.

s9.title: 9. Special case of prospects (account requests)
s9.body: People who submit an account request without yet being a client (via the Request an account page) provide identification and contact data as well as information about their investment project. This data is processed for the sole purpose of reviewing the request. If the request does not lead to a wealth management relationship, it is kept for a limited period, necessary to follow up on the file, then deleted; if accepted, it is incorporated into the client file and follows the retention rules described in section 5.

s10.title: 10. Security
s10.body: {legalName} implements appropriate technical and organisational measures (encryption, access control, distributed locks on financial operations) to protect personal data against unauthorised access, loss or alteration.

meta.title: Risk management & custody of assets · Hentsch Credit
meta.description: How Hentsch Credit manages the custody of assets, the valuation of collateral and the liquidation mechanism.

RiskManagement.title: Risk management & custody of assets
RiskManagement.intro: H. Hentsch Asset Management SA does not execute stock exchange orders on behalf of third parties and therefore does not publish an execution policy or a best-selection report within the meaning of financial market regulation. This page instead describes the real risk management practices applied to the Hentsch Credit platform.

s1.title: 1. Nature of the activity
s1.body: {legalName} acts as an independent asset manager (IAM): it grants crypto-collateralized credit to its clients, against collateral deposited by them, and manages a treasury strategy on tokenized industrial metals and commodities with its own capital. It executes no stock exchange order on behalf of its clients and manages no discretionary securities portfolio on their behalf.

s2.title: 2. Custody and separation of assets
s2.body: Assets deposited as collateral by clients are never used in the company's treasury strategy: the two flows are distinct and never meet at any point. Details of the treasury strategy are on the <link>RWA Strategy</link> page, "Governance & separation of funds" section.

s3.title: 3. Valuation of collateral
s3.body: The value of the deposited collateral is determined from real-time market prices (spot price for tokenized gold, tokenized industrial metals, ETH; 1:1 parity with the dollar for USD stablecoins; spot price for the euro-pegged stablecoin), with no margin or discretionary adjustment applied by the company. This valuation is used both to calculate the credit granted at lock-in and for the daily depreciation monitoring described below.

s4.title: 4. Collateral liquidation mechanism
s4.body: An automatic daily check compares the current value of the collateral to its entry value (at the time of lock-in). A depreciation of 30% triggers an alert visible on the client's account; a depreciation of 50% leads to liquidation of the collateral. Credit already used is not erased by liquidation: it becomes an unsecured claim. Full details, with a worked example, are on the <yieldLink>Yield</yieldLink> page and in the <termsLink>terms and conditions</termsLink>, section 7.

s5.title: 5. Conflicts of interest
s5.body: The company never takes a position contrary to that of its clients on the assets they deposit as collateral: it only receives that collateral, calculates the corresponding credit and, where applicable, liquidates it according to thresholds set in advance and applied automatically and identically to all clients. The company's treasury strategy (industrial metals and commodities) is funded by its own capital, never by assets deposited by clients.

s6.title: 6. Control and audit
s6.body: The risk parameters in effect (credit ratio, rates, liquidation thresholds) are centralised in the platform's credit engine and undergo an automated test suite with every change. Any change to these parameters is logged and never applies retroactively to a position already locked in. Details of the history of these changes are on the <link>Archives</link> page.

meta.title: Collateral yield · Hentsch Credit
meta.description: How gold, silver and ETH deposited as collateral automatically repay up to 60% of your credit, and the liquidation risk in the event of a sharp drop.

Yield.title: The only collateral that repays part of your credit for you
Yield.description: Gold, silver and ETH generate a real yield, automatically reinjected into your credit, up to 60% repaid without lifting a finger.
Yield.eligibleAssetsIntro: Eight assets benefit from the same real automatic repayment-by-appreciation mechanism, not just the gold, silver and ETH highlighted above.

table.notEligible: Not eligible (fixed value or too volatile*)

Yield.shibNote: * SHIB is not a stablecoin but remains excluded from the mechanism: its volatility is judged too high to support reliable recurring repayment.
Yield.dualMechanismNote: Industrial metals and commodities therefore combine two distinct mechanisms: the real automatic repayment described on this page (identical to gold, silver and ETH), and an indicative yield target specific to the bank's treasury strategy on these assets, presented separately and never guaranteed.
Yield.performanceIntro: The real prices of yield-generating assets, over the last 365 days (the maximum available via our market data provider, with no commitment as to their future performance).

example.p1: You deposit $2,000 of tokenized gold (XAUT), at a price of $2,400 per ounce: your collateral represents around 0.833 ounces. At the 350% ratio, a credit of $7,000 is granted to you, and the automatic yield repayment cap is therefore $4,200 (60% of $7,000).
example.p2: The price of gold rises to $2,500 per ounce: the observed appreciation ($100 × 0.833 ounces ≈ $83) is automatically applied to your used credit, on the very day it's observed. This mechanism repeats with every subsequent price rise, until the $4,200 cap is reached.
example.p3: If the price then falls, nothing is taken back from you: the appreciation already applied remains locked in to your credit (a "ratchet" that only ever moves upward). However, no new automatic repayment occurs until the price exceeds the level already reached.
example.p4: Once the 60% cap is exhausted, the remaining credit balance (at least 40%, here $2,800) must be repaid by an explicit contribution from you (deposit or transfer), just like with any other credit.

Yield.timelineIntro: The same example, extended: the price of gold keeps rising over several months, until the 60% cap is reached.
Yield.timelineNote: In month 2, the price drops: no repayment occurs that month, but the $83 already applied in month 1 remains locked in (ratchet). Once the $4,200 cap is reached in month 11, no further automatic repayment occurs on this position, even if the price keeps rising.

liquidation.p1: The mechanism above benefits from a rise in price. A drop is handled separately, by a distinct mechanism: the value of your collateral is compared daily to its entry value (the one observed at the time of lock-in), not to the last price that triggered a repayment.
liquidation.p2: In the event of a depreciation of at least 30% from the entry value, an alert appears on your account, with no other effect. At 50% depreciation, your collateral is automatically removed from the account (liquidated) at its entry value. The credit you had already used is not erased as a result: it remains fully due, now with no collateral backing it. Liquidated collateral cannot be returned, even if the price recovers afterwards.
liquidation.p3: The contractual detail of this mechanism is in our <link>terms and conditions, section 7</link>.

liquidationExample.intro: Let's take the same $2,000 deposit of gold at $2,400 per ounce ($7,000 of credit granted), but this time the price of gold falls instead of rising:
liquidationExample.item1: at $1,680 per ounce (-30%): an alert appears on the account, with no other effect;
liquidationExample.item2: at $1,200 per ounce (-50%): the collateral is liquidated. The $2,000 of collateral and the $7,000 of credit granted are removed from the account. If you had already used $1,500 of this credit (card, internal spending), that $1,500 remains due, with no collateral behind it anymore.

guaranteed.question: Is the yield guaranteed?
guaranteed.answer: No. It depends entirely on the actual price movement of your collateral. If the price never rises above your entry price, no automatic repayment occurs: you then repay the full amount through personal contribution, exactly as with a stablecoin.

stablecoins.question: Why don't stablecoins (USDT, USDC, DAI…) generate any?
stablecoins.answer: A stablecoin is by design pegged 1:1 to the dollar: by definition, it has no appreciation to realise. Repaying it remains just as simple, though, through personal contribution.

frequency.question: How often is automatic repayment calculated?
frequency.answer: Daily, based on the live spot price of your asset, with no action on your part, and visible in your transaction history under the label "Repayment via collateral yield".

ratchet.question: Does the "ratchet" protect me if the price drops?
ratchet.answer: It only protects repayments already applied: they remain locked in, whatever happens next. It does not protect against liquidation, which is triggered relative to your collateral's entry value, not relative to the ratchet (see "The opposite risk" above).

multipleAssets.question: If I deposit several different assets, how does it work?
multipleAssets.answer: Each credit request commits to a single collateral asset, fixed at the time the deposit address is generated. To deposit a second asset, you submit a new request: each position then follows its own appreciation, its own 60% cap, and its own liquidation risk, independently of the others.

history.question: Can I see the history of my automatic repayments?
history.answer: Yes, in your account's transaction history, under the label "Repayment via collateral yield" (a distinct movement from a manual repayment, to remain separately auditable).

RwaStrategy.title: Our investment strategy on industrial metals
RwaStrategy.intro: Beyond precious metals, the bank now accepts tokenized industrial metals and commodities as collateral, and deploys its own treasury strategy on these assets. Here, in full transparency, is how it works and the action plan being followed.
RwaStrategy.apyTargetNote: Target of the bank's own treasury strategy on these assets, not a guarantee, and with no effect on the calculation of your credit. The automatic repayment of your credit remains the one described above: the real appreciation of your collateral, capped at 60%.

cashCarry.title: Cash & Carry Arbitrage
cashCarry.description: Buying the tokenized metal on the spot market, simultaneously selling an equivalent futures contract: the position is neutral to price risk and captures the financing spread (contango).

triangular.title: Collateralization & triangular lending
triangular.description: The tokenized metal is deposited as collateral (a prudent LTV, 50% maximum) with an institutional protocol, to borrow stablecoins reinvested in low-risk treasury funds.

liquidity.title: Selected liquidity provision
liquidity.description: A minority share of the capital feeds targeted liquidity pools, earning a share of the transaction fees paid by market participants.

caseStudy.title: How these figures are obtained
caseStudy.intro: Illustrative example of a $10M treasury deployment on Platinum, at the scale of the bank, not of your individual collateral.
caseStudy.reallocationNote: By reallocating a share of the treasury toward liquidity provision (Pillar C), this net yield can rise up to the 10.2% target, at the top of the 8 to 14% indicative range shown above, with no additional leverage and no guarantee of results.

capital.title: Capital committed
capital.body: This strategy is run on the bank's own treasury, never on the assets deposited as collateral by clients. A client's collateral is used exclusively to secure their own credit (see Yield); it is never lent out or committed to the arbitrage or market making described above.

supervision.title: Supervision
supervision.body: Overseen by the Financial Markets Division, reported to the Investment Committee and Executive Management at every phase change (see roadmap above), with daily internal monitoring of actual performance against the indicative target shown.

usedForStrategy.question: Is my collateral used for this strategy?
usedForStrategy.answer: No. Your collateral remains exclusively allocated to your own credit. This strategy runs on the bank's own treasury, a separate pool of capital.

loss.question: What happens if the strategy loses money?
loss.answer: The loss is absorbed by the bank's treasury, with no effect whatsoever on client accounts or on credit already granted: this risk is never transferred to the client.

targetReached.question: Is the 8 to 14% target already met?
targetReached.answer: It's a medium-term target, not a month-by-month guaranteed result: see the case study above for a detailed example of the net yield calculation.

whyIndustrialOnly.question: Why do only industrial metals have this target?
whyIndustrialOnly.answer: Gold, silver and ETH already benefit from the real automatic repayment described on the Yield page. This indicative target is specific to the treasury strategy on industrial assets, a separate and additional mechanism.

Pricing.description: The rates and fees actually applied by the platform, fixed at the moment your collateral is locked in.

ratio.label: Credit ratio
ratio.detail: Of the amount pledged, at the rate in effect at the time of lock-in.

interestRate.label: Annual interest rate
interestRate.detail: Reference rate (SOFR/EURIBOR) + an 8.5-point risk premium, on the credit used.

originationFees.label: Origination fee
originationFees.detail: Charged once, on the credit issued, at the time the collateral is locked in.

custodyFees.label: Collateral custody fee
custodyFees.detail: On the amount of locked collateral, for as long as the position remains active.

positionDuration.label: Position duration
positionDuration.detail: Renewable; the collateral stays locked as long as the used credit is not repaid.

automaticRepayment.label: Automatic repayment
automaticRepayment.detail: Through the real appreciation of the collateral (gold, silver, ETH, industrial metals). The remaining 40% is repaid through personal contribution.

liquidationThresholds.label: Collateral liquidation thresholds
liquidationThresholds.detail: Depreciation from the entry value: 30% triggers an alert, 50% liquidates the collateral (the credit already used remains due). Details on the Yield page.

Pricing.nonRetroactivityNote: A later change to any of these rates only applies to new lock-ins: a position already opened keeps the rate structure applied to it at creation, until it's repaid or matures.
Pricing.contractualDetail: The full contractual detail of this pricing is in our <link>terms and conditions</link>.
Pricing.exampleIntro: For a deposit of $2,000 ($7,000 of credit granted), fully used for 12 months then repaid, the most conservative scenario (with no reduction from yield).

exampleTable.totalBeforeYieldNote: Excluding any possible reduction from collateral appreciation

Pricing.exampleFooter: Collateral custody fees (0.5%/year) are shown and fixed at lock-in, but their automatic periodic collection is not yet in service at this stage; they are therefore not included in this total. If your collateral generates yield (gold, silver, ETH, industrial metals), part of this $1,085 may be automatically covered, within the limit of 60% of the credit used (see <link>Yield</link>).

earlyRepayment.question: Are there any early repayment fees?
earlyRepayment.answer: No. You can repay all or part of the credit used at any time, with no penalty. Interest only accrues on the duration and amount actually used.

negotiable.question: Is this pricing negotiable?
negotiable.answer: No, it applies uniformly to all clients at the rate in effect at the time of lock-in. A future rate change only applies to new lock-ins.

currencyDifference.question: Why does the rate differ between USD and EUR?
currencyDifference.answer: Each currency applies its own monetary reference rate (SOFR for USD, EURIBOR for EUR) before adding the same 8.5-point risk premium, hence the 1.5-point gap between the two.
